independentDerivation.partA: Since alpha has exact multiplicity r, write P(x)=(x-alpha)^r Q(x), with Q(alpha) nonzero. The product rule gives P'(x)=(x-alpha)^(r-1)[rQ(x)+(x-alpha)Q'(x)]. At alpha the bracket is rQ(alpha), nonzero for the positive integer r over the usual real or complex polynomial setting. Thus precisely r-1 factors of (x-alpha) divide P', not merely at least r-1.
independentDerivation.partB: P'(x)=4x^3-12x-8 and P''(x)=12(x^2-1). A triple root must be among 1 and -1. P'(1)=-16; P'(-1)=0 and P(-1)=0. The given triple root is -1. Independently, expansion verifies P(x)=(x+1)^3(x-3), with cofactor -4 at -1; hence all roots, counted with multiplicity, are -1,-1,-1,3. Both worked and short answers agree.
